summary: New box Part. Pass.: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (115/223)

data.turoyo: Mḥalaqla ruḥa hiya, saliqo ʕal u hno, komər annaqla, šubho l aloho, am mayani mḥalaqqe b feme di ʕayno, nafiqi. Be ma kmo əšne am maye ḥšire ne tamo.
data.translation: Sie sprang oben hinauf, und das Wasser - Gott sei gepriesen! - stürzte in die Mündung der Quelle und kam heraus. Wie lange mochte das Wasser dort eingeklemmt gewesen sein!

rationale: First Detransitive Part. Pass. box: release from a long-standing trapped-water state is explicit; keep the full two-sentence contrast.
115/223 has plural ḥšire plus ne with water as the state bearer, a clear result of confinement. One attestation establishes the new Detransitive section and state box.

summary: Active I confines a person in a room at 71/73 and puts someone in a coercive predicament at 57/71. Both passages are already quoted; no additional copy is needed.
115/223 has inanimate plural water, ḥšire ne, and a long duration. The context contrasts confinement with release, supporting a result state without identifying any agent.
The source has ḥšərli at 71/73 whereas the entry has assimilated ḥšəlli; retain both source spellings without normalizing the existing entry.
Allowed lookup ḥṣr 2 has confinement Detransitive forms, including siege and an imprisoned woman, but ṣ differs from the source's š. Search ḥšir found no existing state box or collocation.
Should ḥšr and ḥṣr 2 receive a semantic cross-reference while retaining their distinct consonants and paradigms?
Confirm whether 71/73 ḥšərli versus inherited ḥšəlli reflects edition spelling or variable r+l assimilation; neither form is silently replaced.
